meaning: Proceedings conducted, or orders passed, in the absence of one of the parties who fails to appear despite receiving lawful summons or notice.
The formal written defence and reply to the plaint or suit filed by a defendant in a civil court proceeding.
Refusal by a bank to pay a cheque, typically due to insufficient funds, stopped payment, or signature mismatch.
The legally prescribed time window within which an aggrieved party must initiate a lawsuit or legal proceeding.
An authoritative document issued by a court or magistrate ordering a person to appear before the court at a specified date and time.
The person or entity named on a cheque or financial instrument to whom payment is directed to be made.
The person who writes and signs a cheque directing their bank to pay the specified sum of money.
A statutory written notice formally calling upon a party to perform an obligation (such as paying a dishonoured cheque amount) within a defined period.
Damages or profits which a person in wrongful possession of immovable property actually received or might with ordinary diligence have received.
A formal written document signed by a client empowering a licensed advocate to act and represent them in a court of law.
The initial statement of claim and legal grounds filed by a plaintiff to institute a civil lawsuit.
An offence in which a police officer may arrest an accused person without a warrant from a magistrate.
An offence where grant of bail is not a matter of right but lies at the judicial discretion of the court.
The entire bundle of essential facts that gives an aggrieved party the legal right to seek a remedy from a court.
A judicial order declaring a summons, notice, FIR, or proceeding legally void and invalid.
A judicial order restraining a party from doing an act (prohibitory) or requiring them to do a specific act (mandatory).
A temporary order passed by a court while the main proceedings remain pending, to preserve the status quo.
A written statement of facts sworn and confirmed by oath or affirmation before an authorized commissioner or notary.
The legal authority and territorial or financial power of a court or tribunal to hear and determine a legal dispute.
The legal standing or right of a person to bring an action or be heard before a court of law.
A formal notice filed in court requesting that no order be passed against the caveator without first giving them notice.
A discretionary order by a court excusing a party for missing a statutory deadline upon proof of sufficient cause.
Under judicial consideration and therefore subject to specific restrictions on public prejudgment or interference.
